thread.title: UNC Health Care working with Apple on new iPhone feature

author: Jennifer Henderson
title: UNC Health Care working with Apple on new iPhone feature
text: – Staff Writer, Triangle Business Journal Jan 25, 2018, 8:01am EST UNC Health Care is among 12 medical institutions nationwide – and the only one in North Carolina – collaborating with Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) on a beta test for a new feature that would allow users to view medical records in the iPhone Health app. “We’re very excited to be in the group of organizations that Apple has decided to collaborate with,” says UNC Health Care Chief Information Officer Tracy Parham , who is also a registered nurse. If you “think about the number of people [who] have an iPhone,” she says, the new medical records feature on the Health app is really “a game-changer.” It places control of health information in the hands of patients, she says, putting “more data at their fingertips.” Ultimately, the more patients are able to understand their data and use it, “that’s going to circle back to how they interact with providers and systems to improve their health.” It will also allow for patients to “be more independent in their health care.” “In the past, patients’ medical records were held in multiple locations, requiring patients to log into each care provider’s website and piece together the information manually,” Apple states of the new feature. “Now, consumers will have medical information from various institutions organized into one view covering allergies, conditions, immunizations, lab results, medications, procedures and vitals, and will receive notifications when their data is updated.” UNC Health Care declined to comment on how it became one of the 12 medical institutions collaborating with Apple on the beta, and a spokeswoman for Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.
